subject: physics
title: Orbits and satellites
key_idea: Gravity provides the force that keeps planets, moons and satellites in circular orbits. It changes the direction of motion but not the speed, so the velocity changes. For a stable orbit, a change in speed needs a change in orbit radius.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Gravity provides the force that keeps planets and satellites in their circular orbits.

items.meaning: The path of one body around another, held in place by gravity.
A moon, which orbits a planet.
A human-made satellite, which orbits a planet or the Sun.
The resultant force towards the centre of a circular orbit. In an orbit it is provided by gravity.

items: Artificial satellites orbit the Earth or the Sun.

blocks.text: The Moon and the International Space Station both have circular orbits around the Earth. They differ in orbital period, height and speed.

items: Gravity provides the force for circular orbits.
Planets, moons, comets and artificial satellites all orbit because of gravity.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) In a circular orbit the speed stays the same but the velocity keeps changing.

items: Velocity is speed in a given direction.
Gravity acts towards the centre of the orbit, at right angles to the motion.
So gravity changes the direction of motion but not the speed.

items.text: Gravity is a resultant force towards the centre.
The satellite accelerates towards the centre.
The direction of motion keeps changing.
So the velocity changes, but the speed does not.

items: Gravity changes the direction of motion, not the speed.
A changing direction means a changing velocity, so the satellite is accelerating.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) A satellite can only keep a stable orbit at one radius for each speed. This is qualitative: no calculation is needed.

items: A slower satellite moves to a higher orbit, where gravity is weaker.
A faster satellite moves to a lower orbit, where gravity is stronger.

diagram.alt: Pick a change to a satellite's speed to see what happens to the radius of its stable orbit.
diagram.prompt: Pick a change to the satellite's speed
result_labels: Radius of the new stable orbit

options.label: The satellite moves slower
options.explanation: A slower satellite can only stay in a stable orbit at a greater radius, where gravity is weaker.

options.label: The satellite moves faster
options.explanation: A faster satellite can only stay in a stable orbit at a smaller radius, where gravity is stronger.

options.label: The speed stays the same
options.explanation: The orbit stays the same size, but the direction of the velocity keeps changing.

items: If the speed of a satellite changes, the radius of its stable orbit must change.
Slower means a higher orbit. Faster means a lower orbit.

checks.q: State what provides the force that keeps a satellite in a circular orbit.
Explain why the velocity of a satellite in a circular orbit changes while its speed stays the same.
checks.a: Gravity acts towards the centre and accelerates the satellite. This changes its direction of motion but not its speed. A change in direction means the velocity changes.

checks.q: A satellite in a stable orbit moves more slowly. Describe the change to its orbit.
checks.a: The orbit moves to a larger radius (a higher orbit), where gravity is weaker.

exam_phrases: (force of) gravity causes the satellite to accelerate (towards the Earth)
the acceleration causes a change in direction
this changes the direction of motion (but not the speed)
a gravitational / centripetal / resultant force acts on the satellite

mistakes.wrong: Gravity makes the satellite accelerate, which changes its speed.
mistakes.right: The acceleration changes the direction, not the speed. Saying acceleration causes a change in speed loses the mark.

mistakes.wrong: Both the Moon and the ISS orbit the Earth.
mistakes.right: The question asks for another similarity and a difference. Give a similarity such as a circular orbit, and a difference such as the orbital period, height or speed.

blocks.text: The ideas about changing velocity and about radius changing with speed are Higher tier only in this course.

worked_example.question:
The James Webb Space Telescope is an artificial satellite that orbits the Sun at a constant speed.

Explain why the velocity of the satellite changes as it orbits the Sun.
answer_points: A gravitational (centripetal or resultant) force acts on the satellite.
So the satellite accelerates towards the centre of the orbit.
So the direction changes, which changes the velocity.
worked_example.tip: Do not say the acceleration causes a change in speed.

exam_phrases: each planet in its own orbit
dwarf planets, asteroids and comets orbit the Sun
comet orbits are not in the same plane as the planets

mistakes.wrong: Comets orbit the Sun in the same plane as the planets.
mistakes.right: The planets' orbits are in the same plane, but comet orbits are not.

mistakes.wrong: Only the planets orbit the Sun.
mistakes.right: Dwarf planets, asteroids and comets also orbit the Sun. Moons orbit planets.

exam_phrases: (resultant) force is perpendicular to the direction of motion
the (resultant) force is a centripetal force
provided by the gravitational pull of the Sun
no work is done on the planet

mistakes.wrong: The speed is constant because there is no force on the planet.
mistakes.right: There is a resultant force, the gravitational pull of the Sun. It is perpendicular to the motion, so it changes direction only.

mistakes.wrong: The planet is not accelerating because its speed is constant.
mistakes.right: The velocity is changing because the direction is changing, so the planet is accelerating.

worked_example.question:
Read the two statements about planet A:

• The speed of planet A is constant.
• The velocity of planet A is changing.

Explain why these two statements are correct. Write about forces.
answer_points: Speed is constant because the resultant force is perpendicular to the direction of motion (a centripetal force).
No work is done on the planet.
Velocity is changing because the direction is changing.
The resultant force is provided by the gravitational pull of the Sun, which changes the direction of motion.
